text: 🇲🇽✊ "Every child should have a scholarship — every one." In Villa de Álvarez, Colima, Sheinbaum announced 57,519 additional primary students added to the Rita Cetina scholarship for the state, with investment exceeding 650 million pesos. Grades, she said, should not decide who gets help. — Sheinbaum at the Beca Rita Cetina event, Villa de Álvarez, Colima Rita Cetina was a 19th-century Yucatecan feminist educator who founded the first secular school for girls in Mexico. The scholarship in her name now covers school supplies and uniforms for primary students nationwide.
📸 Mañanera del Pueblo — viernes 12 de junio de 2026

🇲🇽🎨 "Every dance is a declaration of our Mexican spirit." Bulmaro Juárez Sánchez, indigenous-language advocate, presented traditional dances from Palmar de Bravo in the "Suave Patria" segment of the morning press conference. — Bulmaro Juárez Sánchez Indigenous dances, he said, are historical resistance and cultural continuity — they survived centuries of erasure and remain how communities tell the world who they are. Said on the day Mexico opened the World Cup before the world.

🇲🇽⚽ The President gave her World Cup ticket to a teenager who won a pull-up contest. "As President: I'd rather give the seat to someone who would not have been able to go, who loves football — particularly to a young woman." — Sheinbaum on skipping the Azteca opener She handed her complimentary ticket to Yolett Cervantes Cuaquehua. Asked about opposition figures who did show up at the stadium, she dismissed any drama: "no political persecution here, against anyone."

🇲🇽🌎 "The Treaty benefits all three countries. All three." Sheinbaum's position going into next week's USMCA review talks: this is not a favor Washington does for Mexico. — Sheinbaum on the T-MEC review Negotiations continue next week with a focus on auto tariffs, amid rising jet fuel prices hitting global air travel. Mexico arrives at the table with $709 billion in exports on the year — a record. Counterparts know it.

🇲🇽✊ "No repression. We don't repress anyone." Sheinbaum on the prolonged talks with the CNTE teachers' union and the protests blocking the Centro Histórico: no force, no crackdown — but no retreat from union democracy either. — Sheinbaum at the morning press conference The CNTE wants the return of corporatist union powers. Sheinbaum reiterated the constitutional mandate: "secret, direct and universal vote" for union representation. The break with the old PRI model is not negotiable.

🇲🇽🏭 Industrial output up 2.1% in April. Exports at a record $709 billion. "Look at industrial activity: in April it grew 2.1%. The second: exports — record, 709 billion dollars." — Sheinbaum at the morning press conference Construction was up over 6-7%. The numbers landed the same day Tourism reported three historic records of its own. Months of forecasts about an economic collapse from Trump's tariffs are not aging well.

🇲🇽🌎 Mexico just set three tourism records in a single month. April 2026: 8.3 million international visitors (+8% vs April 2025), 3.81 million tourists, 1.25 million cruise passengers (+31.5%), and $109.8 million dollars in foreign spending — up 36.4% on April 2025. — Josefina Rodríguez Zamora, Secretary of Tourism Emerging markets are driving the growth: Spain +23%, Colombia +18%, Brazil +14%. The state strategy targets diversified markets and indigenous communities — not the old all-inclusive resort model.

🇲🇽⚽ "Whoever bets against Mexico will always lose — in the stadium, in politics, in life." "Those who love Mexico do well on the field, in life, and in politics." — Sheinbaum, morning of the 2026 World Cup opener Mexico beat its opponent 2-0 in the inaugural match at the Estadio Azteca. Plazas filled in CDMX and across the country, the anthem sung in chorus. She opened the press conference on the celebrations and closed the topic with this line.

🇲🇽🏭 BANXICO: MEXICAN FINANCIAL SYSTEM “SOLID” UNDER FIRE

Banxico’s June Financial Stability Report: stress tests confirm the banking system holds capital and liquidity above regulatory minimums even under severe adverse scenarios. The Macrofinancial Vulnerabilities Index sits below critical limits across financial, real, external and public sectors. The Financial Markets Stress Index in May registered lower than at the close of 2025. Translation — while Trump tariffs, the Iran war, and World Bank doom forecasts pummel the region, Mexico’s banking spine is holding.
